newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's Ansett teams with Singapore Airlines.
newsitem.headline: Australia's Ansett teams with Singapore Airlines.

text.p: Australian airline Ansett and Air New Zealand on Friday teamed up with the one of the world's most profitable carriers, Singapore Airlines, in an alliance billed as the most powerful in the Asia-Pacific.

The three airlines, and Ansett's fledgling Asian operation Ansett International, plan to share each other's capacity and use their new economy of scale to implement joint purchasing, promotion and cargo operations, the four carriers said.
The alliance includes code-sharing, giving the airlines access to each other's flights and boosting the choice of routes and frequency of flights each carrier can offer its passengers.
The alliance is planned to come into effect within a few months, pending government and regulatory approvals.
The announcement follows weeks of speculation about such an alliance, but falls short of an equity partnership.

An Australian newspaper reported this week that Singapore Airlines would take a one-third stake in Ansett Holdings Ltd, the parent company, with a capital injection of over A$200 million (US$150 million).
Ansett is the weakest financially of the alliance partners and such a tie-up is seen as crucial if Ansett is to get its bottom line airborne over the next three years.
Ansett has been trading in the red in recent years and expects to break even in the current year ending June 30.

"Developing a family of strong airline allies in partnership with our bedrock partner, Air New Zealand, is an important part of our plans to restore sustainable Ansett profitability," Ansett executive chairman Rod Eddington said in a statement.
For Ansett, the alliance bolsters its international profile compared with Australian arch rival Qantas Airways Ltd, which is owned 25 percent by British Airways.
